jobs.title: Data Engineer, Operations Technology (all genders)
jobs.description:
Work with HelloFresh in Warsaw and its HelloTech organisation, HelloFresh’s global technology backbone with more than 1000 people, building the digital products that power our end-to-end food experience. From meal kits and ready-to-eat meals to specialty offerings like pet food and premium meat & seafood, HelloTech creates the platforms that bring tailored food solutions to millions of customers every month.

 Our subscription-based, direct-to-consumer model relies on technology at every step, from customer-facing apps and personalization logic to pricing, forecasting, supply chain optimization, and initiatives that help reduce food waste. While our brands operate independently to serve distinct customer needs, they are united by shared platforms, data, and operational excellence built by HelloTech.

 HelloTech works in autonomous, cross-functional alliances, each owning a specific product or domain end to end. By working with our Warsaw office, you will help shape scalable, data-driven products used across our markets, working with a modern tech stack and international teams to continuously improve how people discover, order, and enjoy HelloFresh’s products, today and in the future.

 About the Team

 The Supply Chain Data Engineering team powers the end-to-end operational backbone of HelloFresh across our global markets. Our core mission is to harmonize supply chain data to enable seamless, data-driven decision-making across enterprise domains - including menu planning, procurement, fulfillment, logistics. We build, scale, and maintain the foundational data assets that power critical operational processes and telemetry. Bringing together Data Engineers, Data Scientists, Operations Analysts, and Product Managers, our autonomous, cross-functional team transforms massive operational data streams into actionable intelligence to optimize forecasting, logistics, kitting, inventory, minimize food waste, and ensure the timely delivery of fresh ingredients to millions of customers worldwide.

 About the Role: What's in the Box

 As a Data Engineer in Supply Chain Operations, you will take technical ownership of the end-to-end data lifecycle—spanning system architecture, pipeline design, production development, and continuous operations. You will build and scale high-throughput batch and real-time streaming data pipelines that harmonize data streams across menu planning, forecasting, procurement, fulfillment and logistics.

 In this role, you play a critical part in driving operational efficiency, cost optimization, and supply chain scalability by ensuring our global data infrastructure is performant, resilient, and mission-critical. Partnering closely with Data Scientists, Operations Analysts, and SCM stakeholders, you will model complex physical domain entities and engineer robust data assets that power real-time tracking, analytics, and automated decision-making across HelloFresh's operational business process.

 What You'll Do: The Recipe

 Become an integral part of a high-impact engineering team supporting global supply chain, procurement, and logistics operations.

 Design, build, and maintain robust batch and streaming data pipelines connecting procurement systems, warehouse management systems (WMS), and logistics networks.

 Model complex supply chain domains—including recipe component sourcing, inventory turnover, fulfillment batching, and route optimization—into clean, scalable analytical datasets.

 Develop real-time data integrations for tracking ingredient inventory levels, order assembly status, and carrier shipment tracking across distribution centers.

 Partner with Data Scientists and Operations Analysts to operationalize demand forecasting models, waste reduction algorithms, and safety stock optimizations.

 Ensure high data quality, freshness, and lineage tracking for operational dashboards, executive KPIs, and automated logistics alerts.

 Work with modern cloud data technologies such as AWS (S3, EMR, Glue, Redshift), Apache Spark/PySpark, Kafka, Airflow, Snowflake, and Databricks.

 Collaborate closely with cross-functional stakeholders in Procurement, Fulfillment Operations, Logistics, and Product to turn physical workflow requirements into data infrastructure.

 Contribute to a collaborative and knowledge-sharing environment, providing technical guidance and coaching to team members and stakeholders.

 Work beyond your specialization when the problem demands it. Your specialization is your anchor, not your boundary.

 Operate what you build. You instrument, monitor, and improve your systems in production. Shipping is the beginning of the learning cycle, not the end.

 What You'll Bring: The Ingredients

 Hands-on experience working with AI tooling (e.g., Claude Code, Cursor, Copilot) beyond casual experimentation. You use AI agents every day. You have a practical sense of how the context you provide to AI tools shapes output quality, and how to set boundaries on AI-generated work.

 Proven track record of scientific or engineering work (Bachelor's, Master's, or PhD) in computer science, software engineering or related field.

 3+ years of work experience as a Data Engineer, including delivery of production data.

 Fluency in Python, SQL, and PySpark for building scalable ETL/ELT data pipelines on a modern cloud data infrastructure.

 Strong data modeling expertise (dimensional modeling, relational architecture, event-driven data streams) applied to physical supply chain or logistics operations.

 Experience with software development practices and tools such as Git, CI/CD, Docker, and AWS.

 Exceptional communication capabilities to bridge technical implementation details with warehouse operators, logistics planners, and business stakeholders.

 You take full ownership. You have a bias to ship. You finish the last twenty percent. 

 You have product sense and are opinionated about what should be built and why, and you can back that opinion with data and user evidence.

 Above all, we are looking for people who will make HelloFresh better. There are many different ways of developing skills, and we love diverse experiences! So even if you don’t “tick all the boxes” but think you’d thrive in this role, we would really like to learn more about you.

 What we offer: The Toppings 

 Global collaboration at scale: Collaborate with experienced engineers and product partners across HelloTech’s international teams, in a culture of active knowledge sharing.

 Technology with real-world impact: Build and operate modern systems at global scale, supporting 6+ millions of customers and complex supply chain operations.

 Technical/Product/Design leadership: Drive best practices and influence architecture/design, quality, and ways of working in an autonomous, product-led setup.

 End-to-end development/delivery: Drive decisions from problem definition to production, improving systems and enabling long-term scalability.

 Access to workspace at Warsaw Centre Point. The hub offers modern facilities including showers, breakout zones, outdoor space, cycle parking, and refreshments (coffee, soft drinks, and fruit).

 Are you the missing ingredient? If this sounds like a tasty opportunity, we’d be excited to hear from you. We aim to review your profile and respond within 5 business days.

jobs.title: Senior Data Platform Engineer, Intelligent Platforms (all genders)
jobs.description:
About the role

 At HelloFresh, data is at the heart of everything we do — from the moment a customer places an order to the way we forecast demand, optimize our supply chain, and personalize experiences for millions of people. Making that data fast, reliable, and available is what our Data Platform makes possible.

 We are looking for a Senior Data Platform Engineer to join our Operational Data Platform team — the squad that ensures operational data is created, delivered, and shared downstream reliably, cost-efficiently, and with the quality guarantees that everything downstream depends on — so the analytics layer receives quality data, ready to be turned into governed assets. You will build the streaming, messaging, and self-service provisioning systems that hundreds of backend and data engineers rely on every day.

 This is a hands-on engineering role at the core of our platform. You'll own critical infrastructure, drive efficiency, and help define the "golden path" that makes it effortless for engineers across the company to store and stream their data — with governance and cost control built in from the start.

 What you'll do

 Build and run our streaming and messaging platform. Own the systems that move data in real time and at scale — Kafka, Kafka Connect, Flink, and SQS — and keep them fast, resilient, and easy to build on.

 Drive efficiency. Identify and act on opportunities to reduce the cost and complexity of the platform, and make efficiency a default rather than an afterthought.

 Own the reliability of critical data paths. Keep the systems at the heart of the platform highly available, and continuously improve their resilience, observability, and operational maturity.

 Enable self-service for operational data stores. Build and maintain the Terraform modules and tooling that let engineering teams use the right database for their use case within minutes, with governance and cost guardrails out of the box.

 Build AI-powered self-service. Develop tooling — including AI and agent-based capabilities — that lets teams operate and maintain their own data infrastructure, so the platform runs without us in the loop.

 Raise the bar on data quality for operational data, including data quality checks on Kafka, so downstream analytics can trust the data from the moment it's created.

 Collaborate across the platform. Work closely with the Analytical Data team so high-quality operational data flows seamlessly into the analytics platform through clean, well-defined handover points.

 Operate what you build. Participate in on-call rotations for the systems you own, and invest in automation so the platform runs without a human in the loop.

 What you'll bring

 Hands-on experience as a data, software, or platform engineer , with a track record of building and operating production data infrastructure at scale.

 Strong software engineering fundamentals and proficiency in a backend language (e.g., Go, Java, Scala, or Python ).

 Deep experience with event streaming and messaging systems — Kafka in particular — including their operational characteristics in production.

 A solid understanding of databases (relational and NoSQL — e.g. PostgreSQL, MongoDB, DynamoDB) and the trade-offs between them.

 Experience building infrastructure on AWS with infrastructure-as-code ( Terraform ), containers, and Kubernetes.

 A strong ownership mindset — you care about reliability, efficiency, and the developer experience of the teams you serve.

 Comfort with on-call responsibilities and a bias toward automating away toil.

 Excellent communication skills and the ability to collaborate across engineering teams to design seamless, composable services.

 Nice to have

 Experience with Flink , stream processing, Kafka Connect.

 Experience building self-service developer platforms .

 Familiarity with data lake architectures.

 What we offer

 Compensation & Financial Wellbeing 

 You’ll receive a competitive salary package, including a HelloFresh-subsidized pension scheme.

 Enjoy savings on your weekly HelloFresh box.

 Save with discount schemes with corporate benefits and Vorteile.

 Health & Wellbeing 

 Support your mental wellbeing with access to platforms like Headspace and Spill.

 Stay active with 24/7 office gym access, a discounted Urban Sports Club membership, and other wellbeing resources.

 Flexibility & Work-Life 

 Balance your life with our flexible hybrid model.

 Recharge with sabbatical leave options in addition to standard time off.

 Get to work with ease through sustainable travel perks and transportation benefits.

 Career & Development 

 Embrace "Learning Never Stops" with internal training, the HelloFresh Academy, and a dedicated budget for German language courses.

 Culture & Environment 

 Enjoy tasty in-office meal deals and fresh food options.

 We support working families with parent-friendly policies, an in-office kids corner, and an on-site babysitter.

jobs.title: Digital Analytics Engineer
jobs.description:
Here at Hometap, we’re collaborative, passionate, and always ready to roll up our sleeves to create solutions that help people get more out of homeownership — and out of life. Our first product, a home equity investment, gives homeowners the opportunity to quickly access the equity they’ve built in their home to pay for what’s most important to them, from handling debt to finally making much-needed renovations, without taking on debt. 

 We work hard, and have some fun along the way, too. You don’t have to take our word for it: The Boston Globe and Forbes have recognized us as a great place to work, and we’ve been honored for our commitment to innovation in the fintech space by Inc. , HousingWire , and more! 

 In case you need any more convincing, we also provide competitive compensation, healthcare coverage, generous PTO, a meaningful equity package, and a strong culture with plenty of opportunities for team-building and camaraderie.

 Interested in joining us on our mission to make homeownership less stressful and more accessible? We’d love to talk.

 Who you are: 

 As a Digital Analytics Engineer, you'll own how Hometap captures and governs its product and marketing event data. Today we track roughly 200 product events, and you'll be the person who manages that ecosystem by owning the event taxonomy and tracking plan, to keep the data flowing into our downstream tools trustworthy. You'll sit on the data engineering and analytics team and work closely with marketing, product, and engineering - all of whom interact with this data to make decisions.

 This is a role for someone early in their analytics engineering career who cares about data quality, can turn messy tracking into a clear system, and is comfortable partnering across teams to get instrumentation right.

 What you'll do: 

 Audit the current Segment inventory, consolidate duplicates and naming drift, and establish a governed object-action naming convention

 Build and maintain the tracking plan, keeping it to a navigable size, and deprecating events deliberately as the product changes.

 Stand up enforcement so standards are gated

 Configure and manage Segment Protocols for schema validation and violation handling, and manage the sources feeding downstream tools

 Advise on our hybrid capture model with product and engineering; determine if events should be server-side, client-side, or both

 Partner with marketing, product, and engineering on what gets tracked and what it means, and translate their requirements into well-formed event specs

 Document tracking standards, interact with teams so they instrument consistently, and run a review process for proposing, approving, and deprecating events

 Build automated monitoring for schema conformance, event volume, and property completeness that catches naming drift, type mutation, and alert on shift before it corrupts downstream metrics

 What you bring: 

 2+ years of experience in a Data Analyst, Data Analytics, or similar role

 Experience with Segment or a similar customer data platform. Familiarity with the broader analytics landscape like Amplitude, Mixpanel, PostHog, or GA4 is a plus

 A solid grasp of event taxonomy and tracking-plan concepts, including object-action naming, controlled vocabularies, and property typing

 SQL proficiency and comfort querying data in a cloud data warehouse

 Working knowledge of JSON Schema and JavaScript

 Familiarity with Git and CI/CD, and the instinct to treat tracking like code by wiring validation and tests into the pipeline

 Ability to explain tracking standards clearly to marketing, product, and engineering partners and align non-technical stakeholders on why governance matters

 The salary range for this role is $110,000 - $120,000, depending on your experience, skills, location, and other factors. You’ll also receive meaningful equity, so you can share in our growth and success. We offer generous medical, dental, and vision coverage, a work-from-home stipend, parental leave, and plenty of paid time off to recharge.
 Hometap is on a mission to make homeownership less stressful and more accessible. Our home equity investment product provides homeowners with a fast, simple, and straightforward way to access the equity in their home without taking out a loan or having to sell. By investing alongside homeowners, Hometap offers debt-free cash in exchange for a share of their home’s future value — all without any monthly payments over the life of the investment. Through a combination of financial innovation and best-in-class customer service, Hometap enables people to get more from homeownership so they can get more from life.

 Hometap believes that our differences are what bring us together, and one of our biggest priorities is creating a diverse workplace that welcomes and values each team member’s unique perspective, background, and ideas. All roles here are filled based solely on candidates’ qualifications and our business needs. 

Hometap is an equal opportunity employer. We provide employment opportunities regardless of race, age, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender, gender identity, gender expression, genetic information, national origin, pregnancy, marital, veteran, or disability status. If there is an accommodation that would support your ability to apply and interview with Hometap, please let us know by emailing work@hometap.com.

jobs.title: Senior Software Engineer - Core Video & Data
jobs.description:
At Hudl, we build great teams. We hire the best of the best to ensure you’re working with people you can constantly learn from. You’re trusted to get your work done your way while testing the limits of what’s possible and what’s next. We work hard to provide a culture where everyone feels supported, and our employees feel it—their votes helped us become one of the Top 100 Inspiring Workplaces .

We think of ourselves as the team behind the team, supporting the lifelong impact sports can have: the lessons in teamwork and dedication; the influence of inspiring coaches; and the opportunities to reach new heights. That’s why we help teams from all over the world see their game differently. Our products make it easier for coaches and athletes at any level to capture video, analyze data, share highlights and more.

Ready to join us?

 Your Role

 We're hiring a Senior Software Engineer to join our Core Data team in London.

 This team builds the systems that power how Hudl understands sport at scale. From identifying players and teams across thousands of leagues to processing the moments that become highlights, stats and analysis, our services sit at the center of Hudl's platform.

 As a Senior Engineer, you'll help shape the technical direction of the Global Sports Library (GSL), the backbone that connects identities, metadata and game context across Hudl products. You'll design and evolve APIs, distributed systems and large-scale data pipelines that ensure Hudl products operate from a consistent understanding of the game.

 This role is deeply backend-focused and comes with significant ownership. You'll tackle complex engineering challenges around scalability, entity resolution, data consistency and platform architecture, while helping raise the technical bar across the team through design leadership, mentoring and pragmatic decision-making.

 The systems you build won't support just one product or one sport. They'll become shared capabilities used across Hudl's ecosystem, powering experiences for teams, athletes and fans around the world.

 Be a key technical leader. You'll support the team by breaking down complex engineering problems, advocating for best practices and guiding others in addition to your focus on delivery.

 Maintain efficiency. You'll ensure your team delivers high-impact work efficiently by focusing on outcomes over outputs. Your leadership will empower the team to make data-driven decisions and iterate quickly on feedback.

 Collaborate across disciplines. You'll work closely with leaders from various disciplines to plan and deliver enhancements across our product suite. Your ability to integrate diverse perspectives will be key to driving innovation.

 Foster Agile practices. You'll participate actively in Scrum ceremonies and play a significant role in maintaining a strong team culture.

 Location 

 Time spent collaborating with your teammates in-office will be a regular part of how you work. We're currently considering applicants within commuting distance of London. You'll be expected to work more days in-office than remote, but will have the freedom to coordinate your specific in-office schedule with your team.

 Must-Haves

 Strong technical proficiency. You have extensive experience in full-stack engineering and have spent time with cloud-based systems and services. You're also an advocate of TDD and CI/CD.

 Technical coaching experience. You're comfortable translating requirements, creating architectural proposals and guiding other engineers through implementation.

 A collaborative, team-first mindset. You know building excellent software is a team effort and you're willing to pitch in whenever a teammate needs a hand.

 Mentor mentality. You believe in the multiplier mindset and enjoy helping fellow engineers hone their skills through code reviews and pair programming.

 Nice-to-Haves

 Tech stack knowledge. Professional background in C#, GraphQL, Elastic, MongoDB and AWS is ideal.

 Experience with media at scale. You've worked with video encoding and on-demand rendering in a professional setting.

 Passion for sports. You have an interest in the sports world and an understanding of sports analytics is a definite plus.

 Familiarity with hybrid teams. You've worked with hybrid or remote teams before and can adapt quickly to our working environment.

 Our Role

 Champion work-life harmony. We'll give you the flexibility you need in your work life (e.g., flexible vacation time above any required statutory leave, company-wide holidays, remote work options and more) so you can enjoy your personal life too. Plus, every five years, we give you a paid sabbatical to unplug and recharge.

 Guarantee autonomy. We have an open, honest culture and we trust our people from day one. Your team will support you, but you'll own your work and have the agency to try new ideas.

 Encourage career growth. We're lifelong learners who encourage professional development. We'll give you tons of resources and opportunities to keep growing.

 Provide an environment to help you succeed. We've invested in our offices, designing incredible spaces with our employees in mind. But whether you're at the office or working remotely, we'll provide you the tech you need to do your best work.

 Support your wellbeing. Depending on location, we offer medical and retirement benefits for employees—but no matter where you're located, we have resources like our Employee Assistance Program and employee resource groups to support your mental health.

 Compensation
 The base salary range for this role is displayed below— starting salaries will typically fall near the middle of this range. 

 We make compensation decisions based on an individual's experience, skills and education in line with our internal pay equity practices. 

 This role will also be eligible for a long-term incentive (LTI) award. Any bonuses awarded are based on individual and company performance paid at Hudl's discretion. 

 Base Salary Range
 £66,000 — £111,000 GBP

Hi! We’re hipages, an ASX-listed tech company and Australia’s #1 digital platform connecting households with trusted home improvement businesses. We're on a mission to transform the home improvement industry to build better lives for everyone.

 You'll play a crucial role in supporting the hipages marketplace by developing our analytics engineering capabilities. Working alongside a talented data team to create immense value for the business and contribute to the development and execution of hipages' commercial strategy.

 One team culture with our teams in Australia, New Zealand, the Philippines and Vietnam

jobs.title: Data Platform Engineer
jobs.description:
Hubble Network was founded with the intention of delivering on the promise of what Internet-of-Things (IoT) was supposed to be. We're building a global Bluetooth® network dedicated to machine-to-machine connectivity. We differentiate ourselves as the first modem-less and gateway-less, direct-to-satellite network from off-the-shelf Bluetooth® Low Energy chips. Hubble is ideal for applications in logistics, AgTech, and maritime where economies of scale for volume consumer and enterprise asset tracking is a priority. Our goal is to be the first billion-endpoint-connected network in the world.

 Hubble is an early-stage, venture-backed startup supported by some of the best investors in the world. In their previous lives, the founding team has been successful in raising $100s of millions in venture funding, developing the Amazon Sidewalk network, launching billions of dollars of space assets, and leading their teams to successful exits, both through acquisition and IPO. We are now looking to bring on talented team members who are the best at what they do to help us make Hubble a reality for the world.

 This is a hybrid, full-time position based in San Francisco, CA. 

 ABOUT THE ROLE 

 This is the founding data hire as the Data Platform Engineer. You will build Hubble's data platform from the warehouse layer up, make decisions on architecture, determine processes for managing schema and data models, and work with many stakeholders.

 We know what we want: a layered lakehouse with Landing, Staging, Warehouse, Mart stages. Each layer has an owner, a purpose, and a quality bar. You’ll work with the Infrastructure team to manage the pipes: Fivetran, Redshift, orchestration, monitoring. You own everything downstream of raw: the transformations, the models, the metric definitions, the quality gates, and the performance bar. 

 The guiding principle is data democratization. Every person at Hubble should be able to answer their own questions. Success is not how many queries you run for other people, it's how few they need you to run. You'll be a peer to Platform Engineering and to the team building our internal operations platform. You'll be an embedded consultant to Finance, Product, and Customer Success. You’ll think about how to present a strong story from data. We expect you to use AI agents as part of how you work, and data work rewards this more than most: schema exploration, model scaffolding, test generation, and documentation are all places where agentic tooling earns its keep if you review the output critically.

 KEY RESPONSIBILITIES 

 Own the transformation layer end-to-end: Defined models across Staging, Warehouse, and Mart. Star-schema design, SCD2, and data contracts enforced by tests at every layer.

 Build the data layer our internal tools run on: mart tables designed for specific operational workflows, sitting behind a generated internal metrics API. You own the mart and the API's performance characteristics; Engineering owns the framework and the frontend. Hold the line at p95 under 5 seconds on mart queries and under 500ms on metric endpoints.

 Make freshness a commitment, not an aspiration: core data and critical operational metrics streamed in real time with Apache Iceberg, with monitoring that catches breakage before a stakeholder does.

 Instrument the funnels: Design event collection across our different product surfaces, unified into a customer 360 spanning authentication, usage, and billing. Acquisition, activation, engagement, retention, revenue.

 Data in space: We collect large amounts of telemetry from our satellites which is critical to mission operations - help our Mission Operations group land this telemetry in dashboards and monitoring systems so they can take action on data immediately.

 Automate revenue reconciliation: Daily comparison of Stripe Platform billing against Hubble usage, with discrepancies flagged before month-end and drill-down to the device and packet level. Turn a multi-day manual close into a few hours.

 Define metrics once: Active devices, packet volume, MRR, contract utilization. Every number has a canonical definition, an owner, and visible lineage from source to dashboard. “Which revenue number is correct?” should stop being a question anyone asks.

 Implement classification in the pipeline: Security defines the tiers and the guardrails. You tag datasets by sensitivity, enforce retention, masking, and anonymization, and keep lineage and access logs auditable. Hubble does not store PII, and the pipeline is where that commitment either holds or quietly fails.

 Build for self-service: Semantic layers that let business users work with customers and revenue rather than join keys, curated datasets, a data catalog, and documentation good enough that people stop asking you.

 Choose boring technology: Fivetran, dbt, Redshift, Metabase are all options - we lean towards buy over build. Bring a strong opinion about which is which, and be able to defend it.

 AN IDEAL CANDIDATE HAS 

 Critical Thinking: You interrogate a metric request before building it, because the question behind it is often different from the question asked. You spot the difference between a data quality problem and a source system problem, and you fix upstream when you can. You make decisions with incomplete information and revise them as you learn.

 Partnership: You work as a peer to Platform and Engineering, with clear ownership boundaries and no throwing work over the wall. You sit with Finance and Product long enough to understand what they're actually trying to decide. You disagree constructively and commit fully once a decision is made.

 Ownership & Pragmatism: You've shipped a data model you later had to tear out, and you learned something specific from it. You explain lineage and trade-offs to people who don't write SQL. You know when to ship the imperfect table that unblocks a decision this week and when to slow down and get the grain right.

 BASIC QUALIFICATIONS 

 7 + years building production data systems, with 2+ years at senior or staff scope owning architecture rather than executing someone else's.

 Deep SQL and dimensional modeling: star schemas, slowly changing dimensions, grain discipline. You can explain fact tables and grains.dbt (or similar) in production: model organization, macros, incremental strategies, tests as contracts, and CI that blocks bad merges.

 Cloud data warehouse depth, ideally Redshift (or similar): distribution and sort keys, vacuum and analyze behavior, workload management, and the ability to take a slow query apart and make it fast.Python or Scala for the specialized pipelines: custom connectors against proprietary APIs, backfills, and reconciliation jobs.Event and product analytics instrumentation: you've defined a tracking plan, argued about event taxonomy, and built funnel tables that survive contact with a changing product.

 Data quality as engineering: anomaly detection, freshness monitoring, and incident response with real escalation paths.

 You've been paged for a broken pipeline and you've fixed the class of bug, not the instance.

 Fluency with AI agents in your own workflow: you already use agentic coding tools to ship real work, and you have a point of view on where they help and where they quietly introduce errors that only show up three models downstream.

 Experience with high-volume machine-generated data, telemetry, events, or IoT at billions of rows, where your partitioning and incremental strategy created a cost-efficient and performant data product.

 Semantic layer and metric definition work: you've built the abstraction that keeps one number meaning one thing across every tool.

 Streaming or near-real-time ingestion (Kinesis, Kafka, Redpanda) with Apache Iceberg or Pinot and a clear view of when it's warranted and when a scheduled batch is the honest answer.Ownership of a BI tool as a platform: permissions, curated collections, and the discipline that keeps a Metabase instance from becoming an unmaintained graveyard . 

 STRONGLY DESIRED 

 Interest or experience in IoT, satellite systems, telemetry, or geospatial data.

 Billing, usage-based pricing, or revenue reconciliation and recognition workflows.

 SOC 2 or similar compliance work: classification frameworks, access reviews, audit evidence.

 Open source contributions or public technical writing.

 COMPENSATION & BENEFITS 

 💰 Salary: $153,000 - $250,000 (commensurate with experience)
🩺 Comprehensive Benefits – Health, Dental, Vision, & HSA options
🌍 Unlimited PTO
🚇 Commuter Benefits (if working from HQ)
🎓 Learning & Development Allowance
💪 Health & Wellness Stipend
🌎 Sabbatical Program – Recharge and explore new ideas
🛠 Cutting-Edge Space Tech – Work on state-of-the-art satellite system

 The posted compensation range reflects multiple levels within Hubble Network's Talent architecture. Final level placement and corresponding compensation will be determined through the interview and assessment process, taking into consideration factors such as the candidate's relevant experience, qualifications, skills, and geographical location. 

 ITAR REQUIREMENTS 

 Hubble is required by the U.S. Government to comply with various space technology export regulations including the International Traffic in Arms Regulations (ITAR). All applicants must be U.S. citizens or lawful permanent residents (“green card holders”) as defined by ITAR (22 CFR §120.15). More information on ITAR can be found here .

 Hubble is committed to creating a diverse environment and is proud to be an equal-opportunity employer. Each individual has the right to work in a professional environment that promotes equal employment opportunity and prohibits discriminatory practices, including harassment. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, gender, gender identity or expression, sexual orientation, national origin, genetics, disability, age, or veteran status.

jobs.title: Senior Data Engineer
jobs.description:
About Hopscotch Primary Care 

 At Hopscotch Primary Care, we believe great healthcare should be accessible to all people across all communities. Today, almost 20% of Americans live in a rural community, yet only 11% of physicians practice in those same communities. We are on a mission to transform healthcare in rural America. We provide high-quality primary care tailored to meet the needs of our patients through our robust care model and comprehensive care team, delivering care in our clinics, and across settings, and wrapping resources around the patients who need them most. 

 Our patients and the care teams who serve them sit at the center of everything we do at Hopscotch. Hopscotch Primary Care takes a team approach to serve patient needs and provide the best care possible. Our goal is to provide the care each of us would want for ourselves or for our family members, in the right setting, and at the right time. 

 Today, we are serving thousands of patients in our value-based care model and the number is growing every day. If you want to bring your experience, skill and passion to make a lasting impact in healthcare, we’d like to meet you. 

 ABOUT THE ROLE

 We are looking for a Senior Data Engineer (remote) to own and evolve the backbone of our data platform. This role is for a hands-on builder who thrives at the intersection of data engineering, software architecture, and pragmatic problem solving. You’ll design and scale the systems that ensure our data is trustworthy, accessible, and ready to power everything from day-to-day operations to next-generation AI applications. While this is not a people manager role, you will serve as a technical leader on the team, raising the bar on engineering fundamentals and helping shape the long-term direction of our data ecosystem. You will be part of a skilled, passionate, and collaborative team committed to working together to realize Hopscotch’s ambitious and important vision. 

 RESPONSIBILITIES  

 Architect, build, and maintain our data model, data pipelines, and data access layer that support our care delivery, operations, and analytics in collaboration with the data platform team. 

 Own the end-to-end lifecycle of data pipelines that enable key business operations, support third-party integrations, and ensure timely, accurate data delivery across internal and external platforms.

 Ensure data quality & governance : implement practices that make our data trustworthy and usable for all stakeholders, from clinicians to operators. 

 Monitor and optimize data infrastructure : troubleshoot issues, improve system performance, and drive efficiency through automation and process enhancements. 

 Lead with technical depth : review code and set engineering best practices across the team. 

 Think big picture : design today’s infrastructure with tomorrow’s needs in mind, laying the foundation for high quality workflow enhancements as well as advanced analytics and AI.

 Contribute where business needs are highest: flex across the stack, from backend data engineering to occasional contributions in frontend applications that bring data to life

 Collaborate with cross-functional teams : work with product managers, analytics, operations, and care delivery stakeholders to translate business needs into scalable data solutions. 

 ABOUT YOU

 You would be a great fit for this position if you: 

 Have an ownership mentality; take high-level business and technical challenges, frame them into actionable work, and deliver solutions with minimal oversight.

 Are customer-focused with a passion for serving patients and providers who make healthcare possible

 Are results-driven, focusing time and resources against the most important priorities

 Comfortable with ambiguity and bring a structured, proactive approach to executing

 Energized by building relationships and finding creative solutions

 Articulate and succinct with communication about complex concepts, both verbally and in writing

 From a cultural perspective, you are:

 Agile, yet thoughtful, and can work effectively in a fast-paced, ever-changing environment · Constantly seeking ways to simplify and improve how things are done, bringing a positive attitude to challenges

 Always looking for ways to modernize our stack, testing out the limits of new technologies, and applying new technologies to solve problems where applicable

 Accountable, holding yourself, and others, to a high standard

 Supportive of teammates and aim to share knowledge with others

 Willing to roll up your sleeves to get work done and collaborate effectively with people of all backgrounds

 ADDITIONAL QUALIFICATIONS

 Bachelor’s degree in computer science, engineering, or related field

 4+ years of professional experience in data engineering and software architecture shipping production level code, preferably in healthcare services

 Strong programming skills (Python, Pyspark, or similar) with proven experience in building and scaling reusable, testable, and maintainable data pipelines

 Experience designing and optimizing data models, warehouses, and/or lakehouses

 Familiarity with modern data platforms and cloud ecosystems (ex. Palantir Foundry, DBT, Databricks, Snowflake, AWS/GCP/Azure).

 Track record of ensuring data quality, governance, and reliability

 Ability to balance high-level architecture with tactical execution

 In accordance with the Illinois Pay Transparency Act, we’re providing the full salary range for this position. Actual compensation will be determined based on location, relevant experience and qualifications. Most offers will fall within a portion of the listed range. This position has a salary range of $140,000-170,000 annually, based on location, relevant experience and qualifications. In addition to base salary, we offer a comprehensive benefits package that includes:

 Paid holidays + PTO

 Company sponsored medical, dental, and vision insurance for you + your family

 FREE short-term and long-term disability insurance

 FREE $100k life insurance policy

 401k plan with 4% company match + no vesting period

 $720 - $1,000 added to employee Health Savings Account annually for eligible health plans

 And more!

 At Hopscotch Primary Care, we embrace diversity, invest in a culture of inclusion and positivity and encourage all to apply to join our team. You will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, gender, gender identity or expression, sexual orientation, national origin, genetics, disability, age, or veteran status.

About Us: Inca Digital is a veteran-owned data and intelligence company specializing in digital-asset analytics for exchanges, financial institutions, regulators, and blockchain ecosystems. Our technology and expertise provide clarity across crypto markets, tracking blockchain transactions, liquidity movements, and illicit finance, helping clients identify risk, enhance transparency, and improve decision-making. Inca’s infrastructure fuses structured and unstructured data from blockchains, exchanges, social networks, and financial markets. The result is a powerful analytics engine that supports ecosystem monitoring, market surveillance, and counter–illicit finance intelligence across digital-asset networks. Inca operates as a fast-paced, nimble, global, and remote technology company. We leverage an asynchronous‑first workflow, try to minimize time spent on meetings, and believe in open debate and logic over authority. Work alongside some of the sharpest minds in the world, including intelligence analysts, defense veterans, data engineers, quant researchers, linguists, and more.

 Areas of Work 

 Design, build, and operate end-to-end batch and incremental ETL/ELT pipelines , turning raw data into production-grade APIs, dashboards, and automated alerts.

 High-throughput data acquisition from diverse sources: relational databases, third-party and vendor APIs, flat files, blockchain nodes and indexers , and social and web text at scale.

 Develop NLP pipelines working with unstructured and semi-structured text data — entity and claim extraction, classification, deduplication, and enrichment feeding downstream risk models.

 Case management, report generation, and intelligence portal supporting data systems.

 Partner with the Head of R&D, engineers, data scientists, and our investigations team to translate intelligence requirements into scalable client-facing products.

 Contribute to technical design and architecture in a written, argued design process.

 Support improving system data quality and system maintenance: versioning, validation, lineage, reconciliation, and freshness monitoring.

 What We Require 

 3+ years of professional experience developing backend services with Golang

 Good knowledge of Go fundamentals, including concurrency, testing, etc

 Experience with REST APIs and/or gRPC

 Experience working in AWS environments

 Experience with messaging systems such as Kafka/RabbitMQ/SQS/etc

 Experience with SQL databases such as PostgreSQL

 Experience with NoSQL databases such as MongoDB/Redis/DynamoDB

 Familiarity with microservices and distributed systems

 Experience with Docker, Git, and CI/CD

 Nice to Have 

 Experience with Terraform

 Experience with Kubernetes

 Familiarity with observability tooling and practices

 Why join us? 

 We operate in a fully remote, high-trust environment, and we prioritize impact and delivered results over hours logged.

 We offer competitive compensation paired with a comprehensive benefits suite, including medical, dental, vision, and 401(k).

 We invest in our people through childcare and wellness stipends and dedicated employee assistance resources.

 Join a thought leader at the intersection of national security and digital assets, working with cutting-edge tech that defines the field.

 Curious about how we build at Inca Digital? Hear directly from our Head of R&D on how our team builds the infrastructure that powers Inca's intelligence, merging financial, natural language, and blockchain data into custom dashboards and automation tools built around each client's needs.

 🎥 Watch on YouTube: Inside Inca | The Engine Behind Inca's Intelligence 

 Inclusion & Equal Opportunity: As a veteran-owned company, Inca Digital thrives on diverse perspectives, specifically across race, gender, neurodivergence, and veteran status, to solve complex data challenges. We are an Equal Opportunity Employer; all qualified applicants receive consideration without regard to protected status, including disability or national origin.

jobs.title: Senior Analytics Engineer
jobs.description:
About Imagine Worldwide

 All children have immense potential, but hundreds of millions don’t have access to the learning they need. Imagine Worldwide believes that every child should be empowered with the basic right to literacy and numeracy. We provide an innovative education technology solution and implementation model to the global literacy/numeracy learning crisis using the onebillion application and various toolkits and systems to support implementation. Our model is massively scalable, evidence-based, and can deliver foundational learning to millions of the most marginalized children.

 Imagine Worldwide partners with governments, organizations, and communities to provide child-directed, tablet-based learning that is accessible, effective, and affordable. We are incorporated in California (United States) as a nonprofit organization, but operate in Sub-Saharan Africa through locally-registered entities in Malawi, Sierra Leone, and Tanzania. Learn more on our website .

 Role Overview

 The Senior Analytics Engineer builds, runs and improves Imagine’s analytics platform: the infrastructure, pipelines and core data models that the organisation’s reporting and analysis depend on. The central task is to scale the platform as data volumes grow, keeping costs under control without giving up performance. In a small team, that means covering the infrastructure underneath the data as well as the data engineering itself.

 Imagine’s data comes from many sources. The largest is tablets in more than 1,500 schools across Malawi, Tanzania and Sierra Leone, which record learning activity as individual events, adding up to billions of records. These only become meaningful when joined with programme context, such as active schools per term, device allocations and enrolment, and with operational data from inventory and field data collection. Turning all of this into reliable data on a non-profit budget calls for careful decisions about where processing happens and what each workload costs.

 The role reports to the Director of Analytics, who sets the platform’s architecture and technical standards, and works alongside the rest of the Analytics Team. We are looking for someone senior who takes initiative, turns architectural direction into working systems, and brings forward evidence-based proposals for improving them. As the engineer builds context, they take on increasing ownership of the platform’s day-to-day running and technical decisions.

 Key Responsibilities

 The Senior Analytics Engineer’s responsibilities fall into four pillars. The first two cover the platform itself: the infrastructure it runs on, and the pipelines that bring data in from many sources and process it at scale. The third covers orchestration and the core data models that the rest of the Analytics Team builds on. The fourth covers the practices that keep the platform reliable, secure and affordable to run.

 Data Platform and Infrastructure 

 Imagine’s analytics platform runs on AWS and ClickHouse Cloud, with infrastructure managed as code. In a small team, this role carries the infrastructure work that a larger organisation would split across dedicated platform or DevOps staff, limited to the scope of the analytics platform.

 Build and maintain the platform’s AWS infrastructure, including storage, compute, networking, the data catalogue, secrets and access management (S3, EC2, Glue Data Catalog, Lake Formation, IAM, Secrets Manager).

 Manage infrastructure as code in Terraform, keeping environments reproducible, version-controlled and reviewable.

 Administer the ClickHouse Cloud warehouse, including service configuration, user and role management, and monitoring of performance and capacity.

 Host and maintain the team’s self-hosted tools, including Apache Superset for BI and Apache Airflow for orchestration. This covers deployment, upgrades, authentication and availability. The Senior BI & Data Analyst manages the dashboards and content within Superset.

 Contribute to architectural decisions on how the platform evolves, setting out options and trade-offs for review with the Director of Analytics.

 Large-Scale Data Processing and Pipelines 

 Data reaches the platform from application databases, operational systems and field data tools, and lands in an Apache Iceberg data lake on S3. Spark-based processing on AWS Glue does the heavy work before the data moves into ClickHouse for analysis. The aim is to do expensive processing once, as far upstream as practical, so that downstream models and queries stay fast and affordable.

 Build and maintain ingestion pipelines from the platform’s sources, including application databases, APIs and operational systems, using tools such as AWS Glue, Airbyte and AWS Lambda.

 Implement incremental loading patterns that stay efficient and recoverable as volumes grow, landing raw data in the lake in a form that preserves its full history.

 Develop and optimise Spark jobs that process billions of device events into learning sessions and higher-level aggregates, paying close attention to partitioning, skew and compute cost.

 Bring in and model the programme context that gives event data its meaning, such as schools, terms, device allocations and enrolment, and handle how that context changes over time.

 Design and maintain Iceberg tables for performance and cost, including partitioning strategy, file sizing, compaction and snapshot management.

 Validate data at ingestion and surface quality issues early, working with the Analytics Team to trace them back to their source.

 Contribute to evaluating new processing approaches as volumes grow, including moving more work upstream and assessing where streaming would add value.

 Orchestration and Transformation 

 Apache Airflow orchestrates the platform’s pipelines, and dbt transforms data in ClickHouse into the models that reporting and analysis rely on. This role builds and maintains the foundational layers of those models.

 Build and maintain Airflow workflows that coordinate ingestion, processing and transformation, with clear dependencies, retries and alerting.

 Develop and maintain dbt staging and core models in ClickHouse, following consistent conventions for naming, structure and materialisation.

 Implement incremental models for high-volume tables, choosing materialisation strategies and table designs that balance freshness, correctness and cost.

 Write and maintain dbt tests and model contracts for core datasets, so that changes that would break downstream reporting are caught before they reach production.

 Document core models such as learning sessions as agreed definitions, including their lineage, and make clear where a model applies an approximation rather than a direct transformation.

 Work with the Senior BI & Data Analyst on the boundary between core and reporting models, and with the Data Scientist on datasets for research and evaluation.

 Reliability, Cost and Engineering Practice 

 A small team needs a platform that runs predictably and that more than one person understands. This pillar covers the engineering practices that make that possible.

 Build and maintain CI/CD pipelines in GitHub Actions for infrastructure, pipeline and dbt code, including automated checks that stop unsafe changes from reaching production.

 Implement monitoring and alerting across pipelines, the warehouse and hosted tools, so that failures and delays are visible quickly and reach the right people.

 Respond to platform incidents and data issues, carry out root cause analysis, and contribute to the team’s data quality incident process.

 Apply and maintain access controls and security practices across the data lake, warehouse and BI layer, in line with Imagine’s data governance policies.

 Monitor platform costs across AWS and ClickHouse, track the cost and performance of individual workloads over time, and use that evidence to identify savings and prioritise optimisation work.

 Maintain and periodically test backup and recovery procedures for the platform’s core components.

 Take part in code review and write clear runbooks and technical documentation, following the team’s documentation standards, so that knowledge of the platform is shared across the team.

 Requirements

 The qualifications below are grouped by importance. Core requirements are needed to do the role from the start. Strongly preferred skills shorten the time it takes to become effective on Imagine’s platform. Advantageous experience adds value but is not expected. We do not expect any one candidate to bring everything listed here.

 Education 

 A bachelor’s degree in Computer Science, Software Engineering or a related field, or equivalent practical experience. Demonstrated experience is weighted equally to formal credentials.

 Experience 

 At least 7 years in data engineering, software engineering or platform engineering roles, including at least 3 years building and running distributed data processing (Spark or equivalent) in production.

 A track record of taking responsibility for a production data platform, or major parts of one, including its reliability, performance and day-to-day operation.

 Experience working with datasets in the hundreds of millions to billions of records, and designing processing that stays efficient as volumes grow.

 Experience running data workloads within real budget constraints: making deliberate trade-offs between compute, storage and performance, and being able to show the effect of those decisions.

 Experience managing the cloud infrastructure that data workloads run on, not only using managed services.

 Experience in small teams where engineers cover a broad scope and work with limited supervision.

 Experience working with remote teams across multiple countries and time zones.

 Experience in the non-profit, international development or social sector is an advantage but not a requirement.

 Technical Skills: Core 

 Strong Python, written to production standards, with testing and modular design.

 Advanced SQL, including writing and optimising queries against analytical databases.

 Spark (PySpark), including performance tuning for partitioning, shuffles and data skew.

 A solid understanding of data lake design, including columnar formats such as Parquet, partitioning strategy, and when to process in the lake rather than the warehouse.

 Hands-on AWS experience with data services and the infrastructure around them, such as S3, Glue or EMR, IAM and EC2.

 Infrastructure as code, using Terraform, CloudFormation, CDK or similar.

 Linux administration and Docker, to the level needed to deploy and maintain self-hosted services.

 dbt in production, including incremental models and testing.

 Workflow orchestration with Airflow, Dagster, Prefect or similar.

 Git, CI/CD and code review practice.

 Technical Skills: Strongly Preferred 

 Apache Iceberg, or another open table format such as Delta Lake or Hudi.

 ClickHouse, or a comparable columnar warehouse such as Snowflake, BigQuery or Redshift.

 Terraform specifically.

 Apache Airflow specifically.

 AWS Glue and Lake Formation.

 Data modelling for analytics, including handling reference data that changes over time.

 Innodata's Federal Practice builds the trusted data layer for critical infrastructure Trust & Safety work.  As the Data/Annotation Engineer, you'll be hands-on with the data itself. You'll work with the AI Solutions Engineer to ensure the data going into our models is accurate, well-labeled, and fully traceable. This role is for someone detail-obsessed who understands that great AI starts with disciplined, well-governed data.

 Key Responsibilities: 

 Receive, validate, ingest, and ontology-map the ODIN mission-aligned corpus from AFS delivery

 Produce the ODIN load report: corpus description, ontology mapping, readiness state

 Configure CVAT annotation pipeline against the Phase 1 starter kit rule pack

 Operate both self-service and lightweight white-glove annotation paths during Phase D corpus production

 Produce 50–100 label demonstration corpus across synthetic and mission-aligned content

 Support QA/Evaluation Lead on QC execution and corpus annotation dry-runs

 Associate DataCard provenance records with annotated and synthetic outputs in coordination with the Solution Architect

 Must-Have Qualifications: 

 Bachelor's degree in Data Science, Computer Science, or related field preferred. Equivalent experience may substitute for degree on a 2-for-1 basis.

 5+ years total professional experience, 3+ years in data engineering or annotation operations

 Annotated dataset ingest pipelines: schema mapping, format validation, ontology alignment

 Full-motion video (FMV) annotation concepts and tooling

 Python scripting for data wrangling, validation, and format conversion

 Active Secret clearance with TS/SCI eligibility

 CVAT annotation platform — AI feature configuration and operation

 DoD or IC data program experience: CUI, distribution statements, federal data governance

 Evaluation design for AI/ML training data: IAA methodology, drift detection, model performance measurement

 Video understanding or FMV annotation experience

 DataCard or ML data provenance framework familiarity

jobs.title: Associate Data Platform Engineer
jobs.description:
About impact.com

 impact.com is the world’s leading commerce partnership marketing platform, transforming the way businesses grow by enabling them to discover, manage, and scale partnerships across the entire customer journey. From affiliates and influencers to content publishers, brand ambassadors, and customer advocates, impact.com empowers brands to drive trusted, performance-based growth through authentic relationships. Its award-winning products— Performance (affiliate), Creator (influencer), and Advocate (customer referral)—unify every type of partner into one integrated platform. As consumers increasingly rely on recommendations from people and communities they trust, impact.com helps brands show up where it matters most. Today, over 5,000 global brands, including Walmart, Uber, Shopify, Lenovo, L’Oréal, and Fanatics, rely on impact.com to power more than 225,000 partnerships that deliver measurable business results.

 Your Role at Impact: 

 Impact's Data Platform Engineering team is looking for an Associate Data Platform Engineer ready to build real distributed systems skills on large-scale production data. Our platform powers analytics, ML, and data products at TB–PB scale using Scala, Python, Spark, Kafka, Airflow, and BigQuery on GCP.

 This is a foundational role for someone early in their career who wants to learn how serious data infrastructure is built and operated, with mentorship from experienced engineers and clear patterns to follow. You'll work within the Data Analytics Group (DAG) alongside Analytics Engineers, Data Analysts, and Data Scientists, though you won't own dbt models, metric definitions, or reporting. Our ideal candidate has strong programming and SQL fundamentals, genuine curiosity about how systems behave under load, and good judgement about when to ask for help.

 The role reports to the Team Lead, Data Platform Engineering, and is based in Cape Town, hybrid, with two days per week in office.

 The platform: 

 The platform has strong foundations: Scala and Spark pipelines processing TB-scale data, dozens of managed data connectors, Airflow on Astronomer for orchestration, a mature dbt transformation layer, and BigQuery as the core analytical warehouse. You'll also have room to shape the platform's next chapter: modernising parts of the compute stack, and building out governance frameworks, data contracts, SLOs, observability, cost management, and data quality monitoring within your domain.

 What You'll Do: 

 Pipeline development: Build and extend batch and streaming pipeline components under guidance. Write clean, tested Scala and Python code. Add Spark transformation steps, build Airflow DAGs, and implement Kafka consumers with senior support.

 Platform configuration: Configure platform components such as BigQuery tables, partitioning strategies, and Cloud Storage buckets with guidance.

 Observability & data quality: Build monitoring dashboards and alerting for job success, latency, and pipeline health. Implement data quality checks to catch anomalies, schema violations, and missing data.

 Operations & incident response: Shadow the on-call rotation, help investigate root causes, debug using logs, metrics, and traces, and maintain runbooks and operational documentation.

 Security, governance & cost awareness: Follow least-privilege access, secrets management, and PII handling by default. Consider the cost and performance implications of your changes with guidance.

 Collaboration & craft: Use AI coding assistants while holding the same quality and review standards. Participate in code reviews, pairing, and technical discussions, and communicate progress and blockers clearly.

 What You Have: 

 Preferred Requirements: 

 1–3 years of experience in software engineering, data engineering, or a related technical role

 Working programming ability in Scala, Java, or Python, with an appetite to become strong in both Scala and Python

 Solid SQL fundamentals: joins, aggregations, window functions, and an understanding of query behaviour

 Understanding of data structures, algorithms, and software engineering basics, including Git and collaborative development workflows

 Exposure to or eagerness to learn distributed processing (Spark), streaming (Kafka or Pub/Sub), orchestration (Airflow), and a major cloud platform, ideally GCP (BigQuery, Dataproc, Cloud Storage)

 Strong problem-solving instincts and a methodical approach to debugging

 Clear written and verbal communication, suited to an async-first distributed team

 Willingness to participate in on-call learning and operational work

 Nice to Have (Advantageous) Requirements: 

 Internship, academic, or personal project experience building data pipelines

 Exposure to CI/CD, automated testing, or infrastructure as code

 Familiarity with data formats such as Parquet, Avro, or JSON

 Exposure to dbt, Looker, or BI tooling

 Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Engineering, Mathematics, or a related field is a plus

 Experience in the digital marketing technology industry is a plus

 Benefits and Perks: 

 At impact.com, we believe that when you’re happy and fulfilled, you do your best work. That’s why we’ve built a benefits package that supports your well-being, growth, and work-life balance.

 Flexible Working: Our Responsible PTO policy means you can take the time off you need to rest and recharge. We're committed to a positive work-life balance and provide a flexible environment that allows you to be happy and fulfilled in both your career and your personal life.

 Health and Wellness: Your well-being is a priority. Our mental health and wellness benefit includes up to 12 fully covered therapy/coaching sessions per year , with additional dependent coverage. We also offer a monthly gym reimbursement policy to support your physical health.

 A Stake in Our Growth: We offer Restricted Stock Units (RSUs) as part of our total compensation, giving you a stake in the company's growth with a 3-year vesting schedule, pending Board approval.

 Investing in Your Growth: We’re committed to your continuous learning. Take advantage of our free Coursera subscription and our PXA courses.

 Parental Support: We offer a generous parental leave policy, 26 weeks of fully paid leave for the primary caregiver and 13 weeks fully paid leave for the secondary caregiver.

 Technology Financial Support: We provide a technology stipend to help you set up your home office and a monthly allowance to cover your internet expenses

jobs.title: SDE II - Data Engineer
jobs.description:
InMobi (Corporate) 

 InMobi Group is a global technology company shaping the future of agentic commerce and advertising. Through its ecosystem of businesses — including InMobi Advertising and flagship consumer platform Glance — InMobi leverages data, machine learning, and generative AI to help brands reach audiences more precisely and consumers discover products more intuitively. Glance, which is pioneering new models of agentic commerce, is owned and operated by Glance InMobi Pte. Ltd., a non-consolidated subsidiary of InMobi Pte. Ltd.

 InMobi Advertising 

 InMobi Advertising, part of global technology company InMobi, is an agentic advertising platform helping brands and merchants achieve their business outcomes. Through its proprietary intelligence, AI-led solutions, and vast consumer reach — including flagship consumer platform Glance — InMobi Advertising delivers the omnichannel performance defining what's next in advertising and commerce. Glance is owned and operated by Glance InMobi Pte. Ltd., a non-consolidated subsidiary of InMobi Pte. Ltd. To learn more, visit advertising.inmobi.com.

 Glance 

 Glance is an intelligent shopping agent, redefining the commerce experience. Powered by proprietary agentic intelligence and generative AI, Glance delivers a hyper-personalized consumer experience across mobile and TV — shaping the new era of shopping. Glance is operated by Glance InMobi Pte. Ltd., a non-consolidated subsidiary of global technology leader InMobi, and is backed by Mithril Capital, Google and Jio Platforms. To learn more, visit glance.com.

 Role Overview

 We are looking for a hands-on SDE-II – Data Engineer to join InMobi’s Demand-Side Platform (DSP) team. In this role, you will build, maintain, and optimise scalable data pipelines that support programmatic advertising, campaign analytics, audience targeting, and attribution.

 You will work with batch and streaming data, distributed processing frameworks, cloud data platforms, and analytical storage systems to transform large volumes of data into reliable and actionable insights. You will collaborate with backend, product, and ML engineering teams to develop efficient data solutions that support DSP operations.

 This role is ideal for an engineer with strong fundamentals in Python, SQL, and distributed data processing who is keen to solve data engineering challenges involving high-volume event streams, performance optimisation, and data reliability.

 Key Responsibilities

 1. Data Engineering and Pipeline Development

 Develop, maintain, and optimise end-to-end batch and streaming data pipelines for processing events such as bid requests, impressions, clicks, and conversion signals.

 Build data ingestion and transformation workflows using Python, SQL, Apache Spark/PySpark, and relevant data engineering frameworks.

 Work with data lakehouse architectures and contribute to ingestion, storage, transformation, and serving layers.

 Implement data quality checks, schema validation, error handling, and monitoring to ensure data accuracy and reliability.

 Support data modelling and query optimisation for analytical and reporting workloads.

 Contribute to pipeline performance improvements, resource utilisation, and efficient compute and storage usage.

 2. Distributed Processing and Streaming

 Work with distributed data processing technologies such as Apache Spark, PySpark, and Apache Kafka .

 Develop and support streaming workflows for processing event-driven data, with attention to data freshness, reliability, and processing efficiency.

 Implement mechanisms for handling duplicate, delayed, or failed events, including retries, checkpointing, and recovery where applicable.

 Investigate production issues and troubleshoot data pipeline failures, performance bottlenecks, and data quality discrepancies.

 Contribute to the adoption and effective use of technologies such as Apache Flink, Spark Structured Streaming, and open table formats where relevant to the platform.

 3. Data Storage and Analytics

 Work with cloud-based data platforms and storage services to support scalable data processing and analytics.

 Develop and optimise SQL queries, data transformations, partitioning strategies, and table structures.

 Contribute to analytical data stores such as StarRocks, ClickHouse, or similar technologies, based on project requirements.

 Work with data lake table formats such as Apache Iceberg, Delta Lake, or Apache Hudi, where applicable.

 Support data modelling, metadata management, access controls, and data retention practices in line with established engineering standards.

 4. Collaboration and Engineering Practices

 Collaborate with backend engineers, ML engineers, and other stakeholders to understand data requirements and deliver reliable data solutions.

jobs.description:
About Invisible 

 Invisible is an Applied AI research company closing the gap between frontier models and the enterprise. We provide the platform infrastructure that makes AI work in production at scale: unify fragmented data, map complex processes, orchestrate and evaluate agents, and stand up hyper-personalized workflow applications fast for companies like Grubhub, Alliance Global, and Thomson Reuters. Where models fall short, we build RL environments and data to fix them. The result: a virtuous cycle between enterprise deployment and model training.

Recognized as Best Predictive Analytics Platform of the Year at the 2026 AI Breakthrough Awards, Invisible makes AI work.

 About the Role 

 We're looking for a Director of Engineering to set the technical strategy for Data Labs, the team that builds the benchmarking systems, data pipelines, and RL environments behind our AI training engagements. The frontier labs and enterprises we work with are changing how they train, evaluate, and deploy models every quarter. Your job is to see where that market is going and make sure Data Labs is built for it before our clients ask.

 You'll decide which capabilities we invest in, which we standardize into platform, and which we leave to individual engagements. You'll track how training methods, evaluation practices, and data needs are shifting across the industry, and turn that into a technical roadmap and a point of view our commercial and research teams can sell against.

 You'll lead a group of engineering managers, forward deployed engineers (FDEs), and senior ICs, and partner closely with applied research, product, and go-to-market leadership. This is a hands-on strategic role. You won't spend much time writing code, but you'll stay close enough to the technical work to make and defend hard architectural calls, and close enough to clients to know which calls matter.

 What You'll Do 

 Technical Strategy & Roadmap 

 Own the multi-year technical strategy for Data Labs, and translate it into a roadmap tied to where the AI training and evaluation market is heading.

 Decide where to build shared platform versus engagement-specific solutions, weighing reuse against team autonomy so platforms speed teams up rather than creating over-dependency.

 Set architectural direction for benchmarking infrastructure, data pipelines, and RL environments so they stay reproducible, portable across client deployments, and ready for the next generation of training methods.

 Anticipate technical shifts 6–18 months out, such as new post-training techniques, agentic evaluation, and synthetic data, and place the bets that keep Invisible ahead of them.

 Set expectations for how AI is used in design reviews and day-to-day engineering work.

 Market Intelligence & Competitive Positioning 

 Build a clear, current view of how frontier labs and enterprises are training, evaluating, and deploying models, and what that means for the data and infrastructure they'll need from us.

 Track the competitive landscape across AI data, evaluation, and RL environment providers, and help define where Invisible differentiates.

 Turn client signals, research developments, and market trends into investment recommendations for executive leadership.

 Partner with product and commercial teams to shape new offerings, pricing logic, and the technical story behind them.

 Evaluation & Data Strategy 

 Define Invisible's point of view on benchmarking and evaluation, including pre- and post-engagement comparisons, capability gap analyses, and regression tracking.

 Make sure evaluation design ties to client-defined success metrics, validate automated checks against human judgment, and be explicit about what each approach can't see.

 Identify reusable data assets, frameworks, and pipelines that become durable advantages and improve margins across engagements.

 Shape practices for data licensing, privacy, and contamination risk as a strategic differentiator, not just a compliance requirement.

 Client & Executive Engagement 

 Represent engineering in executive conversations, strategic client relationships, and pre-sales, translating technical reality into clear, honest narratives.

 Act as a trusted technical advisor to client research and engineering leaders, bringing back what you learn to inform the roadmap.

 Help leaders weigh client-specific asks against broader platform and business goals, with clear short- and long-term paths.

 Organizational Leadership 

 Lead and grow an engineering org of multiple teams, including engineering managers, senior managers, FDEs, and Staff+ ICs.

 Coach managers to build sound technical judgment and strategic awareness in their teams.

 Build hiring pipelines that reinforce a rigorous, client-focused, strategy-aware engineering culture.

 Make sure the org has the planning, quality, and operational practices it needs to execute on the strategy reliably, delegating day-to-day delivery to strong managers.

 What We're Looking For 

 10+ years in software engineering, with significant experience building ML or AI systems.

 5+ years in engineering leadership, including experience managing managers across multiple teams.

 A track record of setting multi-year technical strategy and making platform investment decisions that paid off commercially.

 Deep, current understanding of the AI training and evaluation landscape, including how frontier labs and enterprises approach fine-tuning, RLHF/RLAIF, and evaluation methodology.

 Hands-on familiarity with LLM training pipelines, deep enough to make and defend architectural decisions.

 Experience building benchmarking, data curation, or RL infrastructure that produced measurable client outcomes.

 Ability to read market and competitive signals and turn them into a technical roadmap and a clear product point of view.

 Strong cross-functional partnership with applied research, product, and commercial teams.

 Excellent executive communication, and confidence acting as a technical advisor in client and pre-sales conversations.

 Nice to Have 

 Prior experience at an AI services firm, applied research consultancy, frontier lab, or enterprise AI product company.

 A visible point of view on the AI data and evaluation market, such as talks, writing, or open-source work.

 Familiarity with data licensing, synthetic data generation, or contamination detection involving client data.

 Experience shaping new product lines or service offerings from a technical foundation.

 Experience leading an org through rapid growth or significant change.

 What’s In It For You 

 Invisible is committed to fair and competitive pay, ensuring that compensation reflects both market conditions and the value each team member brings. Our salary structure accounts for regional differences in cost of living while maintaining internal equity.

 For this position, the annual salary will include a 20% annual bonus and an additional incentive structure. The base salary range for SF/NY are:
 Salary Range
 $252,000 — $300,000 USD 

 Bonus and equity is included in all full-time, non commission offers. Final compensation is determined by a combination of factors, including location, job-related experience, skills, knowledge, internal pay equity, and overall market conditions. Because of this, every offer is unique. Additional details on total compensation and benefits will be discussed during the hiring process.

You can find more information about our geographic pay tiers here . During the interview process, your Invisible Talent Acquisition Partner will confirm which tier applies to your location. For candidates outside the U.S., compensation is adjusted to reflect local market conditions and cost of living.

 What It's Like to Work at Invisible: 

 At Invisible, we’re not just redefining work—we’re reinventing it. We operate at the intersection of advanced AI and human ingenuity, pushing the boundaries of what’s possible to unlock productivity and scale. Ownership is at the core of everything we do. Here, you won’t just execute tasks—you’ll build, innovate, and shape the future alongside world-class clients pushing the boundaries of AI. 

 We expect bold ideas, relentless drive, and the ability to turn ambiguity into opportunity. The pace is fast, the challenges are big, and the growth is unmatched. We’re not for everyone, and we’re okay with that. If you’re looking for predictable routines, this isn’t the place for you. But if you’re driven to create, thrive in dynamic environments, and want a front-row seat to the AI revolution, you’ll fit right in.

While some roles may offer remote flexibility, most positions involve in-office collaboration and are tied to specific locations. Any location-based requirements or hybrid expectations will be communicated by our Talent Acquisition team during the recruiting process.

 Equal Opportunity Statement:
